name: ios-webkit-debug-proxy
why: A door into the remote debugging protocol iOS exposes over USB, letting you talk to Safari's inspector from a desktop.

brief.what_it_is: ios_webkit_debug_proxy (iwdp) is a command-line proxy that takes in the debugging traffic iOS devices expose over USB through the usbmuxd daemon and re-exposes it over websocket. Developers can then send commands to MobileSafari and UIWebViews on real and simulated iOS devices. It serves a device list at localhost:9221, and each device's tabs on its own port (9222 onward). The output is a set of JSON endpoints and websocket URLs that DevTools-style frontends can connect to.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a way for developers to reach MobileSafari and UIWebViews on real and simulated iOS devices from a desktop. It notes that recent Chrome DevTools and Safari's WebKit inspector protocols have diverged, so newer Chrome DevTools no longer works with Safari directly.
brief.how_it_works: The proxy talks to usbmuxd, which handles the USB connection to each attached device, and bridges that to websocket clients. Each attached device gets its own port, assigned first-come-first-serve and preserved across detach and reattach until the proxy restarts. The -f flag selects which DevTools frontend HTML page is served, and -c sets the device-to-port mapping.

commands_seen.context: Windows install via Scoop, after adding the extras bucket. The README also requires the latest iTunes on Windows.

commands_seen.cmd: sudo apt-get install autoconf automake libusb-dev libusb-1.0-0-dev libplist-dev libtool libssl-dev
commands_seen.context: Linux build dependencies from the apt repository. Several other libraries must be built from source at newer versions.

commands_seen.cmd: sudo dnf install autoconf automake libusb1-devel libusb-compat-0.1-devel libtool openssl-devel

commands_seen.context: Run inside the cloned repo before building from source on Linux or Fedora.
Verifies that usbmuxd can see the attached device(s). Requires libimobiledevice-utils.
Starts the proxy with default settings. Ctrl-C quits, and it can run in the background.

Example of pointing the proxy at a specific DevTools frontend with -f. The README notes that clicking links on localhost:9222 is blocked with this frontend, so the URL must be pasted into the address bar.

brief.install_notes: macOS: brew install is the easy path. Windows: install iTunes too, via Scoop. Linux: install apt packages, then build and install libplist, libimobiledevice-glue, libusbmuxd, libimobiledevice and usbmuxd from source. Then run ./autogen.sh, make, and sudo make install. A udev rule installed by that step starts usbmuxd when a device is attached. Fedora can use packaged libraries instead of building them. On the device, you must have at least one open browser tab and Settings > Safari > Advanced > Web Inspector set to ON. The iOS Simulator has to be started before the proxy. Some Rosetta builds on macOS need OpenSSL 1.1 paths exported before building.
brief.standout: It is a bridge rather than a debugger: it lets you attach standard DevTools-style frontends to iOS Safari, and the README points to Firefox DevTools via mozilla/valence as another route. Its port scheme, one port per device with a stable mapping across reconnects, is simple and scriptable through the /json endpoints.
brief.status: Unknown from the README alone. The fetched README has no release date, changelog, or last-commit info, and I did not check the repository's commit or release pages. Troubleshooting entries repeatedly say to use the latest version for iOS 12.2+ and iOS 10+ fixes, and the default frontend URL pins Chrome DevTools 27.0.1453.93, which suggests parts of the docs date from around 2013 to 2015.
brief.caveats: The Simulator must be started before the proxy. Windows needs iTunes. Linux requires building several libimobiledevice libraries from source, and the README lists a -lm link fix, a ldconfig fix, and a Rosetta-specific OpenSSL setup. The default frontend is an old pinned Chrome DevTools URL. https frontend URLs will not work without a shield-icon override. Newer Chrome DevTools is not compatible with Safari's inspector protocol, so you need a Safari-extracted inspector or Valence. Some iOS versions have reported empty tab lists or lockdownd errors. Licensing: Google BSD. Bundled libraries are older pinned versions (libplist 2.2.0, libusbmuxd 2.0.0, libimobiledevice 1.3.0). The README's websocket example link is empty, so use the documented paths instead.
quotes: allowing developers to send commands to MobileSafari and UIWebViews on real and simulated iOS devices.

In recent versions of Chrome and Safari there're major discrepancies between Chrome Remote Debugging Protocol and Webkit Inspector Protocol, which means that newer versions of Chrome DevTools aren't compatible with Safari.
Lastly, always try replugging in the USB cable.
